reason: Re-opened packet.js quran 2 --verse 2.115. After the reports of the several occasions (the qibla, the Negus, supplication) al-Tabari gives his own preferred view (qala Abu Ja'far: wa-l-sawab min al-qawl fi dhalika): God singled out East and West as His to inform His believing servants that He owns them and the creatures between them, and that all of them owe Him obedience, including turning toward the direction to which they are turned; his next line (ma'na al-aya idhan) confirms it. The evidence is verbatim and the paraphrase (believers taught that the creatures between East and West are His and owe Him obedience, facing where He directs) carries no more than his words. The sentence does not touch his separate question of abrogation. day.js: 2:114 condemns whoever forbids the approach to the sanctuaries of Allah, so 'Following a warning against barring worshippers from God's sanctuaries' is accurate context and takes no four words from the key; 'God' now stands outside quotation. verse.js ok (Al-Baqarah 2:115, at 121). entry-check ok, no warnings. No school, comparison or tone issue.
